title: Ring maps out of a field of characteristic p lift along nilpotent ideals of F_p-algebras
statement: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$. Let $D$ be a commutative ring with $p\cdot1_D=0$, let $J\subseteq D$ be an ideal with $J^N=0$ for some integer $N\ge1$, let $\pi:D\to D/J$ be the quotient map, and let $g:K\to D/J$ be a ring homomorphism. Then there is a ring homomorphism $f:K\to D$ with $\pi\circ f=g$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0320 (lemma-formally-smooth-extensions-easy, line 44409), part (3): a separable field extension is formally smooth (Definition Tag 00TI, definition-formally-smooth, line 37805: lifting along square-zero ideals), applied to K over F_p, which is separable because F_p is perfect (Definition Tag 030Y, definition-perfect, line 10489; Lemma Tag 030Z, lemma-perfect, line 10495: every element of F_p is a p-th power); the passage from J^2=0 to J^N=0 by lifting successively along D/J^{i+1} -> D/J^i, as in the proof of Algebra Lemma Tag 07K4 (lemma-smooth-strong-lift, line 38291). Used in Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FG (smoothing.tex lines 2468-2470, 2489-2490, 2496-2497). Tags verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: *Algebra structures.* Since $K$ has characteristic $p$, its prime subfield is $\mathbf F_p=\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z\subseteq K$, and $K$ is an $\mathbf F_p$-algebra in a unique way. Every ring $E$ with $p\cdot1_E=0$ (here $D$ and its quotients $D/J^i$, $i\ge1$) has exactly one ring map $\mathbf F_p\to E$, namely $n\bmod p\mapsto n\cdot1_E$, so it is an $\mathbf F_p$-algebra in exactly one way, and a quotient map $E\to E/I$ is a map of $\mathbf F_p$-algebras. A ring homomorphism from $K$ or from such an $E$ to such a ring sends $n\cdot1$ to $n\cdot1$, hence is a homomorphism of $\mathbf F_p$-algebras; conversely every $\mathbf F_p$-algebra homomorphism is a ring homomorphism. So below 'ring homomorphism' and '$\mathbf F_p$-algebra homomorphism' between these rings are the same thing.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0320 (lemma-formally-smooth-extensions-easy, line 44409) applied to K over F_p (the identification of ring maps with F_p-algebra maps is implicit in the citers, Smoothing Ring Maps proof of Lemma Tag 07FG, and Algebra Lemma Tag 0329)

proof.text: *Square-zero case.* By [lem-weil-pbc-field-char-p-h1-cotangent-vanishing], $H_1(L_{K/\mathbf F_p})=0$ (naive cotangent complex of the canonical presentation $\mathbf F_p[K]\to K$). The module of differentials $\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}$ is a $K$-module, i.e. a $K$-vector space, hence a projective $K$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-projective]. So the ring map $\mathbf F_p\to K$ satisfies both hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-square-zero-lifting] (with $A=\mathbf F_p$, $B=K$), which gives, with step 1: (*) for every commutative ring $D'$ with $p\cdot1_{D'}=0$, every ideal $J'\subseteq D'$ with $J'^2=0$, with quotient map $q':D'\to D'/J'$, and every ring homomorphism $g':K\to D'/J'$, there is a ring homomorphism $f':K\to D'$ with $q'\circ f'=g'$. (This is the last line of the proof of 0320 (3), '$K/k$ is formally smooth by Lemma 031Z', for $k=\mathbf F_p$, with 031Z proved as in its source: Proposition 031J and 'a vector space is free (hence projective)'; the vanishing of $H_1$ is the part of the proof of 0320 (3) carried by the cited node, which uses that $K/\mathbf F_p$ is separable as $\mathbf F_p$ is perfect, 030Y/030Z.)

proof.text: *Induction from $J^2=0$ to $J^N=0$.* For $1\le i\le N$ let $\rho_i:D/J^i\to D/J$ be the canonical surjection ($J^i\subseteq J$). Claim $P(i)$: there is a ring homomorphism $f_i:K\to D/J^i$ with $\rho_i\circ f_i=g$. $P(1)$ holds with $f_1=g$. Let $1\le i<N$ and assume $P(i)$. Put $D'=D/J^{i+1}$ and $J'=J^i/J^{i+1}\subseteq D'$. Then $p\cdot1_{D'}=0$, and $J'^2$ is the image of $J^{2i}\subseteq J^{i+1}$ (as $2i\ge i+1$), so $J'^2=0$. By the third isomorphism theorem $D'/J'\cong D/J^i$, and under this isomorphism the quotient map $q':D'\to D'/J'$ becomes the canonical surjection $\sigma_i:D/J^{i+1}\to D/J^i$. Applying (*) of step 2 to $g'=f_i$ (composed with this isomorphism) gives a ring homomorphism $f_{i+1}:K\to D/J^{i+1}$ with $\sigma_i\circ f_{i+1}=f_i$; then $\rho_{i+1}\circ f_{i+1}=\rho_i\circ\sigma_i\circ f_{i+1}=\rho_i\circ f_i=g$, which is $P(i+1)$. Hence $P(N)$ holds. Since $J^N=0$, $D/J^N=D$ and $\rho_N=\pi$, so $f=f_N:K\to D$ is a ring homomorphism with $\pi\circ f=g$ (for $N=1$, $J=0$ and $f=g$).
